rows: Standard investor-conference overview; Celsius framed as a global functional-energy beverage company capitalizing on the shift from traditional to functional/performance energy.
Large addressable market — global energy category to $84.8B by 2025 (~7% CAGR), global functional beverage category over $156B by 2023 (~11% CAGR).
Record $58.2M first-half 2020 revenue (+90%), ~45% revenue CAGR since 2015, $75M FY2019 revenue.
Dual gross-margin presentation — 44.7% as reported / ~52% excluding outbound freight (for comparability to Monster Energy which classifies outbound freight as selling expense).
Distribution is the key growth lever — DSD network at 135 distributors covering ~70-75% of major US metro markets, with key accounts migrating off wholesale/direct in 2021.
Convenience is the biggest opportunity — drives ~70% of energy category volume but Celsius only at 13.8 ACV; long runway ahead.
Broad and aging-up demographic — ~50/50 male/female; consumers aging out of Red Bull/Monster migrate to better-for-you products like CELSIUS.
COVID-19 impaired the gym/health club and vending channels in Q1 and Q2 2020; management expects recovery.
Elevated inventory posture deliberately maintained given COVID supply-chain risk and 100-200% flavor growth rates.
FAST protein snack portfolio (from Func) planned to be seeded in North America in 2021.
Core CELSIUS line drives ~85% of revenue; portfolio includes On-the-Go Sticks, Stevia line, CELSIUS HEAT, CELSIUS BCAA Energy, backed by MetaPlus blend and six clinical studies.
Major shareholders cited — Carl DeSantis and Li Ka Shing.
No question-and-answer exchange took place. The conference host closed the session stating they were out of time for questions. There are therefore no Q&A items to summarize.
